name: HiTech
label: FXHE Records
lede: Fifteen CDs, one storefront demo, and a Detroit ghettotech trio that got Pitchfork's attention and a Coachella stage.

eras.title: Three Detroit rappers, one house
eras.text: Ghettotech is Detroit's fast, filthy mix of techno, bass and rap, and DJ Assault, DJ Godfather and DJ Snowflake are the names its kids grew up on. King Milo, Milf Melly and 47Chops each came up in the city's rap scene first, then decided the club was the job.

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · The FACE: Interview · Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview · Metro Times: How HiTech became · Ableton: HiTech
years.h: King Milo, Milf Melly and 47Chops trade rap for the dance floor
years.p: Each one was already working Detroit's underground rap scene. In Milo's house they started making something built to move people instead.
years.xp:
The origin story changes with the interview. The FADER has Milo and Melly meeting at a [[Babyface Ray|d82481ab-4f2e-4fd7-af2f-9dbaa38704da]] show, The FACE has Milo and Melly going to parties 47Chops threw before they officially met, and Rolling Stone has the three of them coming together through a party where Chops was DJing.

Metro Times has the pivot coming after a bunch of acid trips, in Milo's words: "tired of just rapping". Ableton describes the roles: Milo engineers and mixes, Melly pushes the sound forward, Chops is the DJ and historian.

years.src: Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview · The FADER: The Rap Report · Ableton: HiTech
years.h: Fifteen CDs, and one lands in Omar S's hands
years.p: The debut was a run of 15 CDs, not a release. [[Omar S|b8311533-0e4c-4f90-80a9-ac27d9fc6ac5]] heard it, played it all summer, and signed the trio to his FXHE label.
years.xp:
According to Rolling Stone, 47Chops met Omar S at a storefront show and handed over a demo. Omar S kept it in rotation through the summer and then signed them to FXHE Records.

Milo recalls the pitch in Rolling Stone as "put the turbo boosters on our back" and "let's bring Detroit home".

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: HiTech reissued on FXHE, with a video for "Henny Runtz"
years.p: The self-titled debut that started as 15 CDs got a proper release on Omar S's Detroit label in summer 2022, per The FADER.
years.xp: Metro Times dates the debut to 2021 (the CD run); The FADER says it was re-released on FXHE in summer 2022. We use 2022 for the FXHE release.

years.h: Bruiser Thanksgiving show puts them on Danny Brown's A&R's radar
years.p: Metro Times says Dart Parker, the A&R behind [[Danny Brown|960afc67-9c21-46dd-9c7f-ff2b509e3150]], found the group at the 2022 Bruiser Thanksgiving concert.
years.xp: That meeting is where the Loma Vista story starts: the label signed them in 2024, per Metro Times.

eras.title: Détwat
eras.text: A 28-minute record that plays like an argument against sitting down. FXHE put it out in May, and by year-end Pitchfork and The FADER had both put it in their top 50.

years.src: The FADER: Song You Need · Ableton: HiTech
years.p: The first single from Détwat arrived with a video built from footage of the trio opening for NYC rapper MIKE.
years.xp: The FADER described it as rattling along "like listening to podcasts at 1.5 speed but cool". Milo told Ableton it was built with friend $quid and others in the room, and that he slammed the table through a hot mic for percussion.

years.src: Album of the Year: HiTech · The FADER: The Rap Report
years.p: Album of the Year lists the release date as May 26, 2023 on FXHE. Pitchfork's Cameron Cook called it the best ghettotech rager in recent memory.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's review, by Cameron Cook, gave the album 7.4 (score as listed by Album of the Year). Tracks include "ZOOTED", "BIRTHDAY PEARLS", "TEETEES DISPO" and "WHYYOUFUGGMYOPPS", per The FADER.

The FADER called it more hot-blooded, hysterical and unrestrained than the debut.

years.src: The FADER: The Rap Report · Rolling Stone: HiTech Interview
years.h: The mission statement: kill the club's bad manners
years.p: King Milo told The FADER the trio wants dancers to dance, not stand around.
years.xp:
In the same interview 47Chops said: "It's like we're creating some shit at a time where people is looking for some new shit." The FADER also notes they favour Detroit pioneers like DJ Assault and DJ Snowflake.

Rolling Stone adds that the group had already been playing guerrilla-style shows at protests over Atlanta's "Cop City" project.

years.src: Album of the Year: Pitchfork's 50 Best · Album of the Year: HiTech · Kresge Arts in Detroit
years.h: Pitchfork ranks it No. 29 of 2023; The FADER goes No. 10
years.p: Pitchfork gave the album 7.4 and put it at No. 29 on its 50 best albums of 2023. The FADER ranked it No. 10, per Album of the Year.
years.xp: Kresge Arts in Detroit also notes Rolling Stone coverage of the record. The 7.4 is the score for the Cameron Cook review as listed at Album of the Year; it sat between Avalon Emerson's & The Charm (No. 30) and jaimie branch's Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die ((world war)) (No. 28).

eras.title: Detroit's flag-bearers, now with a fellowship
eras.text: With the album acclaimed, the trio picked up a Detroit arts fellowship, a new label and two new songs, while playing London, Paris and Brussels.

years.h: Kresge Artist Fellowship goes to the trio
years.p: Kresge Arts in Detroit lists HiTech as a 2024 Kresge Artist Fellowship recipient.
years.xp: The Kresge page describes the three as self-taught Detroit natives who combined after local success to make the debut.

years.src: Metro Times: How HiTech became · The FACE: Interview
years.h: They sign with Loma Vista, and the old albums go quiet on streaming
years.p: Metro Times reports a 2024 deal with Loma Vista Recordings, where Dart Parker had scouted them. The FACE noted the FXHE albums were not on streaming.
years.xp: Their two FXHE albums were still not on streaming when The FACE ran its London interview, which covered their London debut in the magazine's New Noise series.

years.src: Le Guess Who? · Bandcamp: SHADOWREALM · Stereogum: Stream HiTech's
years.h: "SPANK!" and "SHADOWREALM" arrive, with ZelooperZ on the latter
years.p: Le Guess Who? lists a new single "SPANK!" from September 2024. Bandcamp lists the two-track SHADOWREALM release on November 26, 2024.
years.xp: HiTech played Le Guess Who? in 2024 at a Thursday night curated by Crystallmess. Stereogum named "Shadowrealm" with ZelooperZ as a highlight.

eras.title: Coachella and the mixtape
eras.text: A Detroit-only sound ended up on a Coachella stage, then the festival circuit of Europe.

years.src: Larimar Media · DJ Mag: Recognise 083 · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.p: HiTech played the Sonora stage; Larimar Media quotes Pitchfork calling it one of the weekend's two best sets.
years.xp: DJ Mag pointed out it was a daytime festival slot for a sound made for club floors. Metro Times reports ZelooperZ, G.T. and dancer Queen Gabby joined them.

years.src: Stereogum: Stream HiTech's · Larimar Media · DJ Mag: Recognise 083 · Exclaim!
years.p: Fourteen tracks, most under three minutes. Stereogum's Tom Breihan called it full of "joyously fizzy high-BPM jams".
years.xp:
Guests include ZelooperZ and Na-Kel Smith; Stereogum also names Debby Friday, Larimar Media names George Riley. Milo told DJ Mag mixtapes are "for the culture".

Stereogum notes a 34-second comedy skit on the tracklist.

years.src: Larimar Media · Metro Times: How HiTech became
years.h: Glastonbury, Dekmantel, Roskilde and Movement on the summer run
years.p: Larimar Media lists a festival run across North America and Europe, including Glastonbury, Movement, Dekmantel, Outlook, Roskilde and Green Man.
years.xp: Metro Times had them scheduled for Movement at Hart Plaza in Detroit on Monday, May 26, at 5:45 p.m. Melly told Metro Times about a stretch of flying to Paris on weekends while still working at FedEx.
